items.prompt: What does an n8n error workflow receive when a sibling workflow throws?
options: A structured payload: failing workflow and execution id, the failing node's name/type, the error message, and the item being processed
Nothing — it must poll for failures
items.explanation: The errorTrigger payload carries everything needed to build an evidence-grade failure record — including the input item, which for parse failures IS the bug report. (obj-08-a)

items.prompt: The course's invariant 'a crash is never silence' is implemented as:
options: Error workflow → error receipt (hash-chained like every receipt) + a pre-staged digest line listing the failure among refusals
A cron job that checks workflow health daily
items.explanation: Errors are not second-class events: the same chain, the same digest citizenship, refusals-first. A 04:10 failure and a productive night leave equally checkable records. (obj-08-b)

items.prompt: The judge endpoint is down, so the offline twin (same rules, parity-tested) decides the night's events. What must appear everywhere the twin's decisions are shown?
options: Nothing — the twin is equivalent, so no label is needed
A warning that results may be inaccurate
The label OFFLINE TWIN — the runtime that decided is named, so the reader knows what they are trusting
items.explanation: Degradation is labelled everywhere it appears: a degraded mode presented as healthy is a lie with uptime. The parity tests are what make the labelled twin trustworthy. (obj-08-b)

items.prompt: When is it acceptable for a lab system to present fixture data as live?
options: Never — fixtures are labelled SIM (mode on the run header, receipt, digest); a fixture presented as live is evidence fraud
When the fixtures were built from real pages
When the live source is temporarily down
items.explanation: The mode label exists precisely so that sentence cannot be written by accident: honesty about origin is the difference between a demo and a deception. (obj-08-b)
